SURPRISE: the tools helper that looks like the receipt authority is the one that is not crash-safe.
candidates.caller_count_note: tools/future/_common.write_receipt is the sidecar standard: git grep shows dozens of tools/future/*.py callers (abi_verdicts, abliteration, accelerator_workunits, adaptive_verification, addressing_gap, ane_preboard, ane_probe_lab, autonomy_trial, ...). hcli does not call it. persist.atomic_write_json has many hcli/agentos callers listed under C10/C01.
candidates.merge_safety: UNSAFE. Different contracts (seal/refuse vs crash-safe replace). A merge either drops fsync or drops the foreign-overwrite guard.
candidates.canonical_api_proposal: Keep both. If tools receipts need crash-safety, have write_receipt call persist.atomic_write_text AFTER seal — that is an implementation change, not a DRY of two APIs.
candidates.deletion_opportunity: None as a merge. Optional: make write_receipt use atomic_write_text internally.
candidates.risk: High if Path.write_text is replaced into hcli persist callers, or if persist's last-writer-wins replace is used on a tools receipt path that _refuse_foreign_overwrite currently protects.
